title: Scoped Privileged Access PRD: SAML bridge, RBAC mapping, and HSM escrow clarifications
creator: Aisha Navarro
description: This PRD clarifies a scoped set of security and compliance requirements for Private and Dedicated deployments: focused work to standardize SAML SSO attribute mapping, RBAC role semantics for tenant and operator scopes, audit event schema and retention, and operational requirements for KMS/HSM escrow and emergency rotation. This ticket is intentionally narrow: it covers requirements and acceptance criteria needed for the incoming development sprint that implements the SAML bridge and on-prem HSM integration APIs. It does not include broader onboarding UX or billing concerns.
scope_changes: Initial scope included SCIM user provisioning; stakeholder decision on 2026-03-03 deferred SCIM to a follow-up ticket to keep delivery focused on SSO attribute mapping and RBAC enforcement. Additionally, multi-operator key escrow policy (cross-tenant delegation) was reduced to 'operator-initiated escrow with dual-approval' rather than full delegated escrow in this phase.
requirements: SAML: Support SAML 2.0 SP-initiated SSO and IdP-initiated flows; consume NameID and up to 8 attribute mappings for role and tenant identification.

Attribute mapping: Define canonical attribute keys: 'redwood:tenant_id', 'redwood:roles' (comma-separated), 'email', 'displayName'. Mapping should be configurable per-deployment via an operator YAML manifest.
RBAC: Implement role hierarchy with three built-in roles: tenant_admin, tenant_user, support_operator. Support custom roles via role templates in a follow-up iteration (out of scope for this ticket).

Audit logs: Emit structured audit events for authentication, role assignment changes, key rotations, HSM access, and breakglass activations. Events must include timestamp (RFC3339), actor_id, actor_role, operation, resource_id, request_id, and decision (allow/deny).
Audit retention: Default retention 365 days for private deployments; configurable between 90 and 1095 days. Export endpoint for forensic export in NDJSON format.

KMS/HSM: Support customer-managed keys (CMK) with two modes: soft-wrap (cloud KMS) and hardware-backed wrap (HSM). HSM integration must support asymmetric wrap/unwrap and signed attestation of key generation.

Escrow & rotation: Provide operator workflow for HSM key escrow with dual-operator approval for retrieval. Support emergency rotation API that rotates wrapping keys and rewraps active DEKs with zero-downtime read path.

Operator access: Operator console must require MFA + SSO and enforce breakglass justification; breakglass activations create a high-priority audit event and require post-review comments within 48 hours.

SLOs: Authentication path must have 99th percentile latency < 300ms in-hosted control plane to identity providers within the same region; fallbacks to cached assertions if IdP unreachable (cache TTL 5m).
Testing: Provide integration test harness and sample IdP manifests (Okta, Azure AD, OneLogin) for CI. Acceptance tests must be runnable against a local private deployment umbrella testbed.
acceptance_criteria:
1) End-to-end SAML sign-on: A user from a configured IdP can authenticate and be assigned the correct tenant_id and roles per attribute mapping (test vectors provided).
2) RBAC enforcement: A user with tenant_user role cannot perform tenant_admin operations; policies are validated via an automated policy test suite.
3) Audit completeness: For a defined sequence of actions (login, role-change, breakglass, key-unwrap), the emitted audit events must contain all required fields and be persisted to the configured retention store.
4) HSM wrap/unwrap: Using the test HSM emulator, wrap/unwrap flows succeed and attestations are recorded in an immutable log.
5) Escrow flow: Dual-operator escrow retrieval requires two distinct operator approvals and produces corresponding audit events; retrieval path is disabled by default until dual-approval is completed.
6) Emergency rotation: An emergency rotation request triggers rewrap of active DEKs and preserves read availability for requests in-flight.
7) Configuration: All SAML attribute mappings and RBAC rule bindings are editable via the operator manifest; changes are applied via a rolling operator-config rollout and logged.
8) Security review: Design reviewed and approved by Security and Compliance (see signoff checklist).
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Kickoff meeting with Security, Infra, and Solutions Engineering. Agreed to defer SCIM to follow-up. Action: Security to provide minimum acceptable audit schema by 2026-03-05.
2026-03-05: Security delivered audit schema draft. Infra estimated 6 dev days for audit pipeline changes. Added to estimate.

2026-03-09: Prototype HSM integration validated against emulator; CR needed to support asymmetric wrap API change. Engineering requests minor change to DEK metadata field naming (approved 2026-03-10).

decisions: Defer SCIM provisioning to a separate ticket to meet sprint cadence.
Use YAML operator manifests for attribute mapping configuration instead of a UI-first approach for this phase.
Escrow retrieval requires dual-operator approval; full delegated cross-tenant escrow deferred.
open_questions: Should 'actor_ip' be stored in plaintext in the primary audit store or only in a hardened forensic export? (security asked for plaintext; legal requested minimization)
What rotation cadence should be recommended in default operator docs for customer-managed HSMs? (proposed: 180 days, pending compliance input)
Are custom roles required in this sprint or can templates be sufficient? (decision: defer custom roles)
Do we need an automated escalation when breakglass is used more than twice in 30 days?
